chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Segregated school in Xenia and Miss McCarthy's singing lessons
summary: He attended a colored school though he could have gone to the white one; a visiting teacher taught do-re-mi, which he used to find his place on the horn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: How were the schools in Xenia? (PHONETIC)?
Segregated. Mostly. No, I could have gone to the -- I could have gone to the white school
because I knew a guy who was operating it in the county -- you know --
I could have had my choice but my school was close to home and everything -- so I went to -- it was strictly a colored school I went to. So, --

No. Not really. There was a singing teacher used to come up there from down at the white school. Her name was Miss McCarthy. And she'd come up and -- you know -- teach us singing -- like that -- do, re, me, fa, sol, la, te, do. E, g, b, d, f.
I don't pay any mind to e, g, b, d, f though -- you know. It's -- you know -- the thing like that. Do, re, me, fa, sol, la, te, do is easy for me, so that's the way I learned -- you know.

So I play my songs like that and then my horn that's the way I -- wherever do was at -- you know if it was in E Flat or whatever -- all I had to do was find do -- I could find the rest of it -- you know. It came pretty easy for me. I don't know why, but. All I know is where's do.
You know -- I could play the rest of whatever it is -- you know.
